title: mut.channel_chladni_cymatic_plates
mutation_directive: Cymatics — Chladni nodal patterns — Ernst Chladni's Entdeckungen über die Theorie des Klanges (1787); contemporary realizations: Nigel Stanford 'Cymatics' (2014), Cymatica music visualizer. VISUAL SIGNATURE: Sand particles on a vibrating square plate self-organize into precise geometric figures — concentric squares, rosettes, six-pointed stars, fractal-symmetric grids — at each resonant frequency. Sand on dark metal; pattern snaps from chaos to crystalline order as frequency steps up. TECHNICAL HOOKS for three.js / GLSL: Plate eigenmode for a square: u(x,y) = cos(mπx/L)cos(nπy/L) − cos(nπx/L)cos(mπy/L). Spawn 50k particles on a 2D plane in 3D space; each step, compute |u(x,y,t)| with current (m,n) and move particle along −∇|u| (downhill toward nodal lines where u=0). Add small Brownian jitter so particles don't perfectly collapse. Audio-reactive: tie (m,n) to FFT of a hum. GLSL: render particles as small white dots with motion-blur trail. Slowly cycle through (m,n) modes — pattern morphs. WHY DIVERSE: Pool has flow-based (boids) and wave-interference-based (Riley) particle motion, but no eigenmode-based self-organization. Chladni produces sharp crystallized symmetry, not flow — totally different visual register. Stay faithful to the visual signature; pick whatever three.js primitives are needed (Lines2 / InstancedMesh / SphereGeometry / custom ShaderMaterial) — but the FORM should read as if this artist made it. REF: https://lsacoman.wixsite.com/cymatics/chladni-plate
